intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including toucans and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Explore the lush rainforest surrounding Arenal Volcano on a self-guided or guided trail system featuring 16 hanging bridges suspended high in the forest canopy. Watch for howler monkeys, coatis, toucans, and morpho butterflies while enjoying dramatic views of the iconic Arenal Volcano cone.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Walk
experiences.description: Join a certified naturalist guide for a wildlife-focused walk through Manuel Antonio National Park, one of the world's most biodiverse areas. Spot all four species of Costa Rican monkeys, two-toed sloths, iguanas, and rare birds, then unwind on the park's stunning white-sand beaches surrounded by jungle.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide
experiences.description: Venture deep into Corcovado National Park, dubbed by National Geographic as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Trek through primary rainforest with a certified guide to encounter tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and if lucky, the elusive jaguar. A bucket-list eco-adventure experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked budget shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport's affordable food court (casado plate ~$8-10) or pick up snacks from a convenience store near the resort upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle from the airport to save money (typically $15-25 vs $60+ for private taxi). Exchange a small amount of USD to Costa Rican Colones at the airport for tips and small purchases. Keep essentials accessible in your carry-on for a smooth late-night arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a free self-guided walk along the beachfront to get oriented. Explore the immediate surroundings of the Aegean Bliss Resort, spot shorebirds and early wildlife along the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local town/village on foot or by inexpensive local bus. Browse the sodas (local eateries) and small markets. Pick up a local SIM card for budget data connectivity (~$10-15). Explore any nearby mangrove trails or public beach access points for free wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach — one of Costa Rica's best free attractions. Stroll the beachfront promenade and find a casual soda for a relaxed first real dinner in Costa Rica.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at resort if included, or visit a local soda for gallo pinto (rice and beans with eggs) — a classic Costa Rican breakfast for ~$4-6.
meals.lunch: Pick up fresh fruit from a roadside vendor (~$2-3) and a casado plate at a local soda (~$6-8).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront soda — try arroz con pollo or fresh fish of the day with rice and beans (~$8-12). Enjoy a local Imperial beer (~$2-3).

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to help you recover from the late arrival. Use this day to plan ahead, download offline maps (Maps.me or Google Maps offline), and confirm upcoming activity bookings. February is dry season in most of Costa Rica — expect sunny weather and warm temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along the beach and nearby forest edge. February is excellent for spotting scarlet macaws, howler monkeys, and various tropical birds. Bring binoculars if you have them. Aim to be out by 6:00-7:00 AM when wildlife is most active.
day_by_day.afternoon: Book a budget zip-lining tour through a local operator near the resort area. Many operators offer 8-12 line zip courses for $35-55 per person. Look for group discounts or hostel-board deals. The canopy tour typically lasts 2-3 hours and offers stunning views of the rainforest canopy.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Visit a local farmer's market or pulpería (corner store) to stock up on affordable snacks and drinks. Enjoy a casual dinner at a nearby soda.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto with fresh tropical fruit juice at a local soda (~$5-7).
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch or grab a bocadillo sandwich from a local bakery before the zip-lining tour (~$3-5).
meals.dinner: Try a traditional casado with fresh fish or chicken at a local soda (~$8-10). Fresh coconut water from a roadside vendor for dessert (~$2).

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining in advance or first thing in the morning for afternoon slots. Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing. Bring sunscreen, insect repellent, and a small backpack. Most operators include safety briefings and equipment. Tip your guides (~$5-10) — it's customary and appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or shared shuttle to a nearby national park or wildlife reserve. Manuel Antonio National Park, Carara National Park, or a local reserve depending on the resort's exact location. Arrive early (park opens at 7:00 AM) to maximize wildlife sightings before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. Look for white-faced capuchin monkeys, sloths, coatis, and hundreds of bird species. Hike one of the well-marked budget-friendly trails. Park entrance fees are typically $18-20 for foreigners — well worth it for the wildlife density.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon via local bus. Rest and freshen up, then enjoy a sunset dinner at a beachside restaurant. Reflect on the day's wildlife encounters.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda before departure (~$5-7).
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch (sandwiches, fruit, granola bars) to eat inside the park and save money — food inside parks is limited and overpriced.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a nicer beachside restaurant for dinner (~$12-18 per person). Try ceviche or fresh grilled snapper — a Costa Rican coastal specialty.

day_by_day.notes: Book park entry tickets online in advance — Manuel Antonio especially sells out during peak season (February is high season). Bring at least 2 liters of water per person, sunscreen, and insect repellent. Hire a certified guide at the park entrance for 2 hours (~$20-25 split among a group) to dramatically increase your wildlife spotting success.

day_by_day.morning: Kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding rental along the coastline or in a nearby estuary. Many beach areas offer affordable hourly rentals ($10-20/hour). Paddle through mangroves for excellent bird and crocodile spotting opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling at a nearby reef or rocky point (rent gear for ~$10-15/day). Costa Rica's Pacific coast offers decent snorkeling with tropical fish, rays, and sea turtles during February. Ask resort staff for the best local snorkeling spots.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local town's nightlife scene on a budget. Many beach towns have free live music at bars on Friday evenings. Enjoy a cold beer and mingle with fellow travelers and locals.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie bowl and toast at a local café (~$5-8).
meals.lunch: Beachside soda — try a patacones (fried plantain) plate with beans and cheese (~$5-7).
meals.dinner: Friday night at a local open-air restaurant. Try arroz con mariscos (seafood rice) — a flavorful and filling Costa Rican staple (~$10-14).

day_by_day.notes: Check tide charts before kayaking or snorkeling — conditions are best at mid to high tide. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only to protect the marine ecosystem. February's dry season means calmer Pacific waters, making this an ideal day for water activities. Store valuables securely at the resort before beach activities.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby waterfall or natural swimming hole. Costa Rica has numerous accessible waterfalls reachable by local bus or affordable shared taxi. Many have free or low-cost entry ($3-8). Hike the trail, swim in the natural pool, and enjoy the jungle atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue waterfall exploration or visit a nearby butterfly garden or frog sanctuary (~$12-18 entry). These small eco-attractions offer incredible up-close wildlife encounters with poison dart frogs, morpho butterflies, and other exotic species.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Visit the local Saturday market (feria) if available — great for cheap fresh produce, street food, and local crafts. Pick up affordable souvenirs directly from artisans.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before the day trip — rice, eggs, fresh juice at a local soda (~$6-8).
meals.lunch: Pack lunch for the waterfall trip or eat at a local soda near the attraction (~$6-9).
meals.dinner: Saturday market street food — try chorreadas (corn pancakes), empanadas, and fresh fruit (~$5-8 total for a satisfying street food dinner).

day_by_day.notes: Wear water shoes or sandals with good grip for waterfall trails — rocks can be slippery. Bring a dry bag for your phone and valuables. Saturday markets are typically held in the morning/early afternoon — check local timing. This is a great day to interact with local Costa Ricans (Ticos) and practice some Spanish phrases.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and relaxation morning. Enjoy the resort's beachfront. Take a sunrise swim in the ocean, practice yoga on the beach (many resorts offer free or donation-based sessions), or simply read a book under a palm tree.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided wildlife boat tour through a nearby river estuary or coastal waterway. These tours (~$25-45 per person) are exceptional for spotting American crocodiles, caimans, river otters, Jesus Christ lizards, and dozens of bird species including roseate spoonbills and kingfishers.
day_by_day.evening: Sunday is a great day to join locals at the beach. Many Costa Rican families picnic and play soccer on Sundays. Join a casual beach soccer game, or simply enjoy the festive atmosphere. Find a soda open for Sunday dinner.

meals.breakfast: Lazy Sunday breakfast at the resort or a nearby café. Try a traditional breakfast with tamales if available on Sundays (~$6-9).
meals.lunch: Light lunch before the boat tour — ceviche and patacones at a beachside spot (~$8-10).
meals.dinner: Simple Sunday dinner at a local soda — casado with chicken or beef (~$7-10). Fresh lemonade or a natural fruit drink (refresco natural) to wash it down (~$2).

day_by_day.notes: The midpoint of your trip — use Sunday evening to review your remaining itinerary, confirm any upcoming bookings, and do a budget check. February Sundays on the Costa Rican coast are lively and social. The wildlife boat tour is one of the best value wildlife experiences in Costa Rica — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk. Costa Rica has over 900 bird species — February is excellent for spotting both resident and migratory birds. Join a free or low-cost guided birdwatching walk offered by many eco-lodges and community groups (~$10-20). Toucans, parrots, herons, and tanagers are commonly spotted.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local chocolate or coffee tour. Costa Rica is famous for both, and many small farms offer affordable tours ($15-25) where you learn about sustainable farming practices, taste fresh cacao, and enjoy locally grown coffee. An excellent eco-adventure that supports local farmers.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class or cultural experience at a local community organization (~$20-30). Learn to make traditional Costa Rican dishes like gallo pinto, olla de carne, or tres leches cake. A fun, educational, and delicious evening activity.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the early birdwatching walk — fruit and coffee (~$3-5).
meals.lunch: Lunch included at the chocolate/coffee farm tour, or eat at a nearby soda (~$6-9).
meals.dinner: Enjoy the food you prepared in the cooking class, or head to a local soda for a simple dinner (~$7-10).

day_by_day.notes: Book the chocolate/coffee tour and cooking class in advance — these fill up quickly during high season. Both activities directly support local Costa Rican families and small businesses, making them excellent responsible tourism choices. Bring cash as many small operators don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day eco-adventure: White-water rafting on a nearby river. The Río Savegre, Río Naranjo, or other rivers near the coast offer Class II-IV rapids depending on your experience level. Budget operators offer full-day trips including transport, equipment, lunch, and guide for $60-85 per person — excellent value for an adrenaline-packed experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue rafting adventure — most full-day trips include afternoon runs through the most exciting rapids after a riverside lunch break.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort tired but exhilarated. Hot shower, rest, and a well-deserved hearty dinner. Share stories with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: High-energy breakfast before rafting — eggs, rice, beans, and fruit (~$6-8). Eat at least 1.5 hours before departure.
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch included with most rafting tour packages (typically rice, beans, grilled chicken, and fresh fruit).
meals.dinner: Reward yourself with a slightly nicer dinner — grilled sea bass or shrimp with local sides at a beachfront restaurant (~$14-18).

day_by_day.notes: White-water rafting is physically demanding — ensure you're comfortable swimming and follow all safety instructions from guides. Wear quick-dry clothing and secure sandals or water shoes. Most operators provide helmets, life jackets, and paddles. Don't bring valuables — operators typically have secure storage for phones and wallets. Book through your resort or a reputable local agency.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after yesterday's rafting adventure. Light beach walk, stretching, or yoga. Visit a local pharmacy if needed for any minor aches. Browse a local artisan market for handmade souvenirs — look for carved wood, hand-painted ceramics, and woven goods made by local artisans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Horseback riding tour through the jungle and beach (~$35-55 for 2-3 hours). A classic Costa Rican eco-adventure that takes you through terrain inaccessible on foot. Many tours end with a beach gallop — an unforgettable experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset horseback ride option (if available) or return for a relaxed evening. Visit a local ice cream shop for fresh tropical fruit sorbet (~$2-3). Enjoy the evening breeze on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie and granola bowl at a local health café (~$6-8). Recovery nutrition after yesterday's exertion.
meals.lunch: Casado plate at a local soda before the horseback riding tour (~$7-9).
meals.dinner: Beachside barbecue soda — grilled chicken, plantains, and rice (~$8-11). Fresh watermelon juice (~$2).

day_by_day.notes: Inform the horseback riding operator of your experience level — tours are tailored for beginners through experienced riders. Wear long pants to prevent saddle chafing and closed-toe shoes. Most reputable operators practice ethical animal care — look for horses that appear well-fed and healthy. This is a great day for photography — bring a waterproof phone case or small camera.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby wildlife rescue center or sanctuary (~$15-25 entry). Costa Rica has numerous excellent wildlife rescue centers where injured and orphaned animals are rehabilitated. See sloths, monkeys, toucans, and other native species up close while supporting conservation efforts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby cloud forest or secondary forest reserve on a self-guided or guided hike. Look for tree frogs, leaf-cutter ants, coatis, and exotic orchids. Many community-managed reserves offer affordable guided hikes ($10-20 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Night wildlife walk — one of Costa Rica's most unique experiences. Many eco-lodges and guides offer 2-hour night tours ($15-25) where you spot nocturnal creatures: red-eyed tree frogs, sleeping birds, bats, insects, and sometimes kinkajous or porcupines. Absolutely magical.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Costa Rican breakfast at a soda near the wildlife center (~$5-7).
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the forest reserve — pack sandwiches, fruit, and water from a local pulpería (~$4-6).
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the night walk — quick casado at a local soda (~$7-9). Keep it light for the evening hike.

day_by_day.notes: The night wildlife walk is a highlight of any Costa Rica trip — book in advance as group sizes are limited. Wear dark clothing, bring a red-light headlamp (less disruptive to wildlife), and move quietly. The wildlife rescue center visit is emotionally rewarding and educational — learn about the threats facing Costa Rica's biodiversity and how conservation efforts are making a difference.

day_by_day.morning: Final full eco-adventure day: Mangrove kayaking tour through a coastal estuary. Paddle through the roots of ancient mangrove trees while spotting crocodiles, herons, kingfishers, and iguanas. Many operators offer guided mangrove tours for $25-40 per person including kayak rental and guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free beach afternoon — swim, sunbathe, and soak in your final full day in Costa Rica. Collect any last souvenirs from beach vendors. Try surfing lessons if interested — many beach areas have beginner surfing instructors for $30-45 including board rental.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best local restaurant you've discovered during your trip. Splurge slightly on your last night — order that whole grilled fish or jumbo shrimp plate you've been eyeing all week. Toast to an incredible trip.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast before the kayaking tour — eggs, gallo pinto, fresh juice (~$6-8).
meals.lunch: Beach lunch at a casual soda — fish tacos or a ceviche plate (~$8-12).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — splurge on a nicer restaurant (~$18-25 per person). Try the catch of the day with coconut rice, fried plantains, and a tropical cocktail. Toast with a local craft beer or guaro sour.

day_by_day.notes: Use this last full day to pack any items you've accumulated, settle any outstanding bills at the resort, and confirm your departure logistics for tomorrow. Exchange any remaining Colones back to USD at a local bank or exchange office (better rates than the airport). Back up all your photos. Leave a review for the local guides and small businesses that made your trip special.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise on the beach — wake up early for one last magical Costa Rican sunrise. Take a short farewell walk, collect any last memories, and photograph your favorite spots around the resort. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout is typically 11:00 AM — confirm in advance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange shared shuttle or budget transport back to Juan Santamaría International Airport. Allow plenty of time — aim to arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before your international departure. Browse the duty-free shops for last-minute gifts (coffee and chocolate are excellent budget-friendly Costa Rican souvenirs).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of zip-lining through the rainforest canopy, spotting sloths and scarlet macaws, rafting wild rivers, and experiencing one of the world's most biodiverse countries on a budget. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at a local soda or resort (~$5-7). Savor every bite of this Costa Rican staple.
meals.lunch: Airport food court or pack snacks purchased from a local supermarket for the journey (~$5-10).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip: Shared shuttles to the airport cost $15-30 vs $60-80+ for private taxis — book in advance through your resort or a local agency. Arrive at the airport early — San José's international airport can be busy on weekend mornings. Keep all receipts for any VAT refund claims if applicable. The best souvenir from Costa Rica: locally grown whole-bean coffee available at supermarkets for $4-8 per bag — far cheaper than airport prices. Safe travels and Pura Vida!

day_by_day.morning: No activities — late-night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Light welcome snack or room service if available.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance. Keep first night simple — hydrate, rest, and prepare for the adventure ahead. Exchange some USD to Costa Rican Colones at the airport for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort to recover from travel. Explore the beachfront grounds, take a short walk along the shoreline, and get oriented with the resort facilities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local nature reserve or beach estuary for a self-guided introductory wildlife walk. Look for coastal birds, iguanas, and crabs. Ask the resort concierge for the closest accessible green space.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll on the beach followed by a relaxed dinner at a nearby beachfront restaurant. Enjoy fresh ceviche and a cold Imperial beer — a classic Costa Rican welcome.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Casual soda (local Costa Rican diner) near the resort — try a casado (rice, beans, plantains, and protein) for $8–12
meals.dinner: Beachfront seafood restaurant — grilled fish or shrimp with patacones, budget ~$20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Stay hydrated, apply sunscreen, and confirm your upcoming activity bookings with the concierge. Check travel insurance documents and local emergency contacts.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning depart toward Manuel Antonio National Park for the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Walk. Begin at 7:00–8:00 AM with a certified naturalist guide to spot sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, toucans, and poison dart frogs in peak morning wildlife activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided walk, spend the afternoon relaxing on the pristine beaches inside Manuel Antonio Park (Playa Manuel Antonio or Playa Espadilla Sur). Swim, snorkel, or simply enjoy the stunning scenery. Grab lunch from park-area vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the nearby town, sampling traditional Costa Rican cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant near Manuel Antonio Park entrance — fresh fruit, sandwiches, or a casado for $10–15
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant near resort — try arroz con pollo or fresh sea bass, budget ~$20–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Manuel Antonio Guided Wildlife Walk in advance. Bring binoculars, insect repellent, and good walking shoes. Park entry fee is approximately $20 USD per person. Arrive early — wildlife is most active in the morning. The park has a daily visitor cap.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — optional yoga on the beach, kayaking, or stand-up paddleboarding offered through the resort. Enjoy the coastal environment before heading inland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the scenic drive or private transfer toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 4–5 hours from the central Pacific coast). Stop at a roadside fruit stand along the way for fresh pineapple and mango.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Arenal-area accommodation (arrange a one-night mid-range lodge near La Fortuna such as Arenal Backpackers Resort or Hotel Magic Mountain, ~$60–90/night). Enjoy a warm soak in a local hot spring — Tabacón or Baldi Hot Springs are excellent mid-range options.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before checkout
meals.lunch: Roadside soda or packed lunch during the drive — stop in San José or Naranjo for a quick bite, $8–12
meals.dinner: Dinner at a La Fortuna restaurant — Don Rufino or a local soda, try gallopinto and beef stew, ~$18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel transition day. Confirm your Arenal-area accommodation booking. If not renting a car, arrange a shared shuttle through the resort concierge ($35–55 per person). The hot springs are best enjoyed in the evening when the volcanic backdrop is lit up.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike. Depart by 7:00 AM to explore the Mistico Arenal Hanging Bridges Park. Walk 16 suspension bridges over the rainforest canopy with views of Arenal Volcano. Spot toucans, howler monkeys, and morpho butterflies.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, cool off with a swim at La Fortuna Waterfall (Catarata del Río Fortuna). The 70-meter waterfall is a 20-minute hike down. Refreshing and stunning — a must-see in the region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna town for a relaxed evening. Browse the local artisan market, then enjoy dinner with a view of Arenal Volcano.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your La Fortuna lodge before the hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack at the hanging bridges park — bring energy bars and water, or eat at the park café, ~$10
meals.dinner: Dinner in La Fortuna town — Restaurante Nene's or similar, try whole fried tilapia with rice and beans, ~$15–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Hanging Bridges entry is approximately $28 USD. La Fortuna Waterfall entry is $18 USD. Wear waterproof hiking shoes and bring a change of clothes for the waterfall swim. The hike down to the waterfall is steep — use the handrails. Start early to avoid afternoon crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Depart La Fortuna early and travel north toward Tortuguero (approximately 3–4 hours by shuttle + boat transfer). This journey itself is an adventure — the final leg requires a scenic boat ride through jungle canals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Tortuguero village. Check in to a mid-range jungle lodge (e.g., Manatus Hotel or Laguna Lodge, ~$80–120/night including meals). Take an afternoon orientation walk through the village and along the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Guided evening turtle or wildlife walk along Tortuguero beach (seasonal — February may offer early nesting activity). Alternatively, take a short evening canal paddle with a local guide to spot caimans and night herons.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at La Fortuna lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Caño Blanco or at a village soda before the boat transfer — casado or fresh fish, ~$10–12
meals.dinner: Dinner included at Tortuguero jungle lodge or at a local village restaurant — Caribbean-style rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, ~$15–20

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is car-free — all transport is by boat or foot. Book the shuttle + boat transfer package in advance (~$35–50 per person). Bring cash as ATMs are limited. Pack light for the boat transfer. Mosquito repellent is essential in Tortuguero.

day_by_day.morning: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — depart at 6:00 AM for the best wildlife sightings. Glide through jungle canals spotting caimans, river turtles, Jesus Christ lizards, howler monkeys, sloths, and over 300 bird species including kingfishers and anhingas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to lodge for lunch and a midday rest. Optional visit to the Sea Turtle Conservancy Visitor Center to learn about the park's iconic leatherback and green turtle conservation programs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat ride along the main canal for golden-hour photography and bird watching. Enjoy a communal dinner at the lodge with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the safari — fruit and coffee at the lodge
meals.lunch: Full lunch at the lodge — typically included with lodge packages, Caribbean-style cuisine
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner or local village restaurant — try rondon (Caribbean seafood stew), ~$15–20

day_by_day.notes: The Wildlife Boat Safari is best at dawn — wildlife is most active before 8:00 AM. Wear neutral-colored clothing (avoid bright colors). Bring waterproof bags for cameras. The Sea Turtle Conservancy charges a small entry fee (~$5). February is the dry season in Tortuguero — conditions are generally favorable.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tortuguero — optional early birdwatching walk through the village trails or a kayak rental along the smaller canals for a self-guided exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Tortuguero via boat and shuttle transfer. Travel south toward Monteverde Cloud Forest region (approximately 5–6 hours including transfers). Scenic journey through the Costa Rican highlands.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Santa Elena / Monteverde. Check in to a mid-range cloud forest lodge (e.g., Hotel El Establo or Arco Iris Lodge, ~$70–100/night). Enjoy the cool mountain air — a refreshing contrast to the coastal heat.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Tortuguero lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Stop in Ciudad Quesada (San Carlos) during the transfer — local soda for a casado, ~$8–10
meals.dinner: Dinner in Santa Elena town — Restaurante Morpho or Tree House Restaurant, try heart of palm salad and local trout, ~$18–25

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the Tortuguero departure boat + shuttle combo in advance. The roads to Monteverde are partially unpaved — a 4WD vehicle is recommended if self-driving. Temperatures in Monteverde drop to 15–20°C (59–68°F) — pack a light fleece or jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — the highlight of the trip! Depart early for one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on 10–15 platforms, with cables stretching up to 750 meters. Experience the Tarzan swing and optional Superman cable for thrill-seekers.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the zip-line, visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a guided or self-guided walk through the primary cloud forest. Look for resplendent quetzals, emerald toucanets, and glass frogs in the afternoon mist.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Bat Jungle or Serpentarium in Santa Elena for a unique evening wildlife experience. Enjoy dinner at a cozy mountain restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before the zip-line tour
meals.lunch: Lunch at the zip-line operator's café or a nearby soda in Santa Elena — gallo pinto and chicken, ~$10–14
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in Santa Elena — Café Caburé for chocolate fondue dessert, dinner ~$20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Monteverde zip-line tour costs approximately $45–65 USD per person. Book in advance — tours fill up quickly. The Cloud Forest Reserve entry is ~$25 USD. Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable clothes you don't mind getting misty. The zip-line has weight restrictions (typically 250 lbs / 113 kg max).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided birdwatching walk in the Monteverde Cloud Forest or Santa Elena Reserve (slightly less crowded than the main reserve). Focus on spotting the resplendent quetzal — February is within the quetzal season.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Orchid Garden for a close-up look at the region's extraordinary biodiversity. Optional cheese factory tour at the Monteverde Cheese Factory (La Lechería) — a historic community institution.
day_by_day.evening: Night walk in the cloud forest with a naturalist guide — spot nocturnal creatures including kinkajous, sleeping birds, and various amphibians. Return to lodge for a warm dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the lodge
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near the butterfly garden or at a local café — sandwiches and fresh juice, ~$10–12
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant or local spot — warm soup and traditional Costa Rican stew, ~$15–20

day_by_day.notes: The guided night walk costs ~$25–35 USD and must be booked in advance. Bring a headlamp. The quetzal is most active at dawn — go out before 7:00 AM for the best chance of a sighting. The Monteverde Cheese Factory offers free tastings and sells excellent artisan cheeses.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Monteverde early and travel south to the Osa Peninsula / Puerto Jiménez area (approximately 6–7 hours). This is a long travel day but rewards with access to one of the world's most biodiverse regions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Puerto Jiménez — gateway to Corcovado National Park. Check in to a mid-range eco-lodge (e.g., Cabinas Jiménez or Iguana Lodge, ~$70–110/night). Rest and prepare gear for tomorrow's Corcovado trek.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Puerto Jiménez town on foot. Visit the local pulpería (corner store) for snacks. Enjoy a sunset dinner by the Golfo Dulce waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Monteverde lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in Palmar Norte or San Isidro de El General — local soda, casado, ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Waterfront restaurant in Puerto Jiménez — fresh catch of the day with patacones and salad, ~$18–24

day_by_day.notes: This is a long drive day — consider breaking it up with a stop at Dominical Beach for a 30-minute stretch and swim. Alternatively, take a domestic flight from San José to Puerto Jiménez (SANSA Airlines, ~$80–120 one way) to save time. Confirm your Corcovado permit and guide booking today.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide. Depart Puerto Jiménez by 5:30 AM via boat or 4WD to La Leona or San Pedrillo ranger station. Begin the guided trek through primary rainforest — one of the last remaining old-growth forests in Central America. Spot tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and possibly a jaguar track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the deep jungle trek with your naturalist guide. Swim at a jungle river crossing or coastal beach within the park. Observe the incredible biodiversity that earned Corcovado its National Geographic title as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.'
day_by_day.evening: Return to Puerto Jiménez by late afternoon. Rinse off, rest, and celebrate the incredible day with a hearty dinner. Share stories with fellow trekkers at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast at the lodge before 5:30 AM departure — eggs, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by guide or lodge — sandwiches, fruit, and energy snacks eaten in the jungle
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Restaurante Carolina in Puerto Jiménez or lodge restaurant — grilled meat or fresh fish, ~$20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Entry to Corcovado requires a licensed guide and advance permit reservation (~$15 USD park fee + $35–50 guide fee). Book at least 2–3 weeks ahead as permits are limited. Wear long pants, waterproof hiking boots, and bring plenty of water (3L minimum). Do not approach wildlife. The trek is moderately strenuous — 8–15 km depending on route.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica — leisurely breakfast and last-minute packing. Take a gentle walk along the Golfo Dulce shoreline or do some dolphin-watching from the dock in Puerto Jiménez (spinner and bottlenose dolphins are commonly seen).
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin journey back toward San José for departure. Fly via SANSA domestic flight (Puerto Jiménez → SJO, ~50 minutes) or drive north (~6 hours). If time permits, stop at a souvenir shop in San José's Mercado Central for last-minute gifts — local coffee, chocolate, and handcrafted items.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) for departure. Enjoy a final Costa Rican coffee and a bite at the airport. Depart with incredible memories of cloud forests, volcanoes, jungle canals, and wildlife encounters. ¡Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Puerto Jiménez lodge — fresh tropical fruit, gallo pinto, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Airport or San José restaurant — try a final casado or a chorreada (corn pancake), ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Domestic SANSA flights from Puerto Jiménez must be booked in advance (~$80–120 USD). Arrive at SJO at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Costa Rica charges a $29 USD airport departure tax (usually included in ticket price — confirm with your airline). Bring home locally grown Costa Rican coffee as the perfect souvenir.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including toucans and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Explore the lush rainforest surrounding Arenal Volcano on a self-guided or guided trail system featuring 16 hanging bridges suspended high in the forest canopy. Watch for howler monkeys, coatis, toucans, and morpho butterflies while enjoying dramatic views of the iconic Arenal Volcano cone.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Walk
experiences.description: Join a certified naturalist guide for a wildlife-focused walk through Manuel Antonio National Park, one of the world's most biodiverse areas. Spot all four species of Costa Rican monkeys, two-toed sloths, iguanas, and rare birds, then unwind on the park's stunning white-sand beaches surrounded by jungle.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide
experiences.description: Venture deep into Corcovado National Park, dubbed by National Geographic as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Trek through primary rainforest with a certified guide to encounter tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and if lucky, the elusive jaguar. A bucket-list eco-adventure experience.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight UA arrives at 22:30. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO). Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome cocktail and light late-night amenity platter prepared by the resort upon request.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport lounge pre-departure.
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport lounge.
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity platter and welcome drink provided by Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer 48 hours in advance. Request an early check-in suite ready for late arrival. Keep Day 2 morning light to allow for rest and recovery from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late wake-up. Enjoy a full gourmet breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant. Take a private orientation tour of the resort grounds, beach, and amenities with your dedicated concierge. Relax by the infinity pool or take a gentle stroll along the beachfront to acclimate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling excursion or paddleboarding session arranged by the resort along the pristine coastline. Alternatively, enjoy a 90-minute welcome spa treatment (deep tissue or tropical botanical massage) at the resort's luxury spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's private beach terrace. Multi-course welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring locally sourced Costa Rican cuisine paired with premium wines.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet beachfront breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict with local herbs, freshly squeezed juices, and specialty Costa Rican coffee.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch – ceviche, grilled fish tacos, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: Signature fine-dining at Aegean Bliss Resort – multi-course tasting menu featuring hearts of palm salad, seared mahi-mahi with plantain purée, and passion fruit soufflé. Wine pairing included.

day_by_day.notes: This day is intentionally relaxed to recover from jet lag. Pre-book the spa treatment at least one day in advance through the concierge. Confirm all upcoming excursion logistics with the concierge this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Walk. Depart the resort at 06:00 with a certified naturalist guide for optimal wildlife viewing. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and poison dart frogs in their natural habitat. The park's biodiversity is best experienced at dawn before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-trek picnic lunch on one of Manuel Antonio's pristine white-sand beaches within the park. Swim in crystal-clear waters and relax on the secluded Playa Manuel Antonio. Return to the resort by 15:00 for leisure time. Optional: visit the resort's beachfront cabana for afternoon cocktails.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset sailing excursion along the Pacific coast departing from the nearby marina (arrange through concierge). Return for a candlelit dinner at the resort or a top local restaurant in Quepos.

meals.breakfast: Early 05:30 breakfast at the resort – granola, tropical fruits, and Costa Rican coffee to prepare for the trek.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort kitchen – artisanal sandwiches, fresh fruit, local cheeses, and sparkling water enjoyed on the beach.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Cantina or Restaurante Barba Roja in Quepos – known for fresh Pacific seafood, grilled lobster, and local craft cocktails. Alternatively, private in-resort dining.

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park is approximately 10–15 minutes from the resort area. Book the naturalist guide well in advance as slots fill quickly. Bring biodegradable sunscreen, insect repellent, and binoculars. Park entrance fees are included in the guided tour package.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private luxury vehicle to Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3.5–4 hours from the Manuel Antonio/Quepos area). Enjoy the scenic drive through Costa Rica's central highlands. Arrive at Arenal by late morning and check into a premium lodge or use as a day excursion base.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike. Explore the lush rainforest on a guided trail system featuring a series of suspended hanging bridges offering breathtaking aerial views of the rainforest canopy, Arenal Volcano, and the surrounding lake. Spot toucans, howler monkeys, and exotic orchids. The guided experience lasts approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in natural volcanic hot springs at Baldi Hot Springs or The Springs Resort's exclusive thermal pools, available for premium day guests. Enjoy a private dinner at The Springs Resort's restaurant overlooking Arenal Volcano.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure – full Costa Rican gallo pinto, eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium lodge near Arenal – try Nayara Springs or Kioro Lodge's restaurant for locally inspired cuisine with volcano views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Springs Resort's Las Ventanas Restaurant – elevated Costa Rican and international cuisine with panoramic Arenal Volcano views. Signature dish: slow-braised local beef with yuca and chimichurri.

day_by_day.notes: This is a full-day excursion day. Confirm private transportation 48 hours ahead. If weather permits, Arenal Volcano may be visible – February is generally a drier month offering better visibility. Bring layers as temperatures are cooler at higher elevations. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort the same evening or opt to overnight near Arenal (consult concierge for premium lodging options).

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a slow breakfast and optional sunrise yoga session on the beach (arrange with the resort's wellness team). Alternatively, book a private surf lesson with a certified instructor on the resort's beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private sport fishing charter departing from Quepos Marina – one of the world's premier marlin and sailfish destinations. Enjoy 4–5 hours offshore with a professional crew aboard a fully equipped luxury fishing vessel. Catch and release or keep your catch for the resort chef to prepare.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the day's catch with a private Chef's Table experience at Aegean Bliss Resort. The resort's executive chef prepares a bespoke 6-course dinner using the day's fresh catch and locally sourced ingredients, served on a private terrace with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast – acai bowls, smoked salmon on artisanal bread, fresh pastries, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch aboard the fishing charter – fresh ceviche, cold cuts, tropical fruits, and cold beverages provided by the crew.
meals.dinner: Private Chef's Table at Aegean Bliss Resort – 6-course bespoke tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Sport fishing charters must be booked at least 3–5 days in advance through the concierge. Quepos Marina is one of the best sportfishing destinations in the world. The Chef's Table experience requires 24-hour advance notice and is subject to availability.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day journey to Tortuguero National Park. Depart early via private luxury vehicle to the Caribbean coast (approximately 4–5 hours). Arrive at the gateway town and board a private motorized canoe to Tortuguero village – accessible only by water or air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari. Glide through the jungle canals on a private guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river otters, green iguanas, Jesus Christ lizards, manatees (if lucky), and an extraordinary array of tropical birds including kingfishers and herons. The afternoon light is ideal for photography.
day_by_day.evening: Check into Tortuga Lodge & Gardens or a comparable premium eco-lodge within Tortuguero. Enjoy a welcome cocktail on the jungle terrace, followed by a candlelit dinner at the lodge's restaurant overlooking the canal.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure – light and energizing: yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tortuga Lodge upon arrival – Caribbean-influenced cuisine including rice and beans, grilled fish, and fresh plantains.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tortuga Lodge's open-air restaurant – Caribbean lobster, coconut curry, and local desserts. Accompanied by the ambient sounds of the jungle.

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is a full travel day. Pack light for the boat transfer. February is dry season on the Pacific side but the Caribbean coast may see brief showers – pack a light rain jacket. This is a UNESCO-recognized biodiversity hotspot and one of the world's most important sea turtle nesting sites (nesting season is July–October, so no turtle nesting this visit, but wildlife is still exceptional).

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise canoe or kayak tour through Tortuguero's secondary canals with a private naturalist guide. These narrower waterways offer intimate wildlife encounters – look for poison dart frogs, spider monkeys, and exotic bird species including toucans and parrots. The misty morning light creates a magical atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tortuguero village for a cultural walking tour. Explore the local community, visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center, and browse artisan shops. Return to the lodge for a leisurely afternoon – enjoy the pool, spa treatments, or simply relax in a hammock overlooking the canal.
day_by_day.evening: Night canal tour by boat with a naturalist guide – spot nocturnal wildlife including caimans (eyes glow red in the flashlight), tree frogs, sleeping birds, and insects. Return for a final dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at the lodge – fresh tropical fruits, eggs, toast, and Costa Rican coffee before the morning tour.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge or a local Caribbean restaurant in Tortuguero village – try rondon (traditional Caribbean seafood stew) or jerk chicken.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Tortuga Lodge – 4-course Caribbean-inspired menu with fresh catch of the day, coconut flan, and rum cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Night tours require insect repellent and a red-light headlamp (provided by the guide). The Tortuguero canal system is one of Costa Rica's most pristine ecosystems. Respect all wildlife and maintain silence during tours for the best wildlife encounters.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Tortuguero by private boat and vehicle back toward the central region. Option to take a scenic 45-minute charter flight from Tortuguero airstrip back to San José or directly to Monteverde area (highly recommended to save travel time – arrange with concierge).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Monteverde Cloud Forest region. Check into El Silencio Lodge & Spa or Monteverde Lodge & Gardens (premium eco-lodge). Afternoon at leisure – explore the lodge grounds, enjoy a spa treatment, or take a gentle nature walk on the lodge's private trails.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the lodge's viewpoint terrace with panoramic views of the Gulf of Nicoya and surrounding cloud forest. Dinner at the lodge's restaurant featuring locally grown cloud forest cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Tortuga Lodge before departure.
meals.lunch: En route lunch at a premium restaurant in the Sarapiquí or Alajuela region, or a packed gourmet lunch box from the lodge.
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Silencio Lodge's restaurant or Monteverde's top dining spot, Celajes Restaurant – known for farm-to-table cloud forest cuisine, organic local vegetables, and artisanal cheeses (Monteverde is famous for its dairy).

day_by_day.notes: Charter flight from Tortuguero to Monteverde (via San José) is strongly recommended over road travel to maximize time. Monteverde is cooler and misty – pack a fleece layer and waterproof jacket. Altitude is approximately 1,400 meters above sea level.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour. Experience one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits, soaring through the misty cloud forest canopy on a series of exhilarating cables, including Superman-style lines and Tarzan swings. The circuit offers stunning aerial views of the cloud forest, wildlife, and on clear days, the Pacific coast. Approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a guided afternoon walk with a certified naturalist. The reserve is home to over 400 bird species including the resplendent quetzal, 100+ mammal species, and thousands of plant species. This is one of the world's most biodiverse ecosystems.
day_by_day.evening: Night walk in the cloud forest with an expert guide – discover the nocturnal world of Monteverde including glass frogs, tarantulas, kinkajous, and olingo. Return to the lodge for a warming dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast at the lodge before the zip-line tour – eggs, gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and Monteverde specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Caburé in Santa Elena – known for handcrafted chocolates, fondue, and creative Costa Rican fusion dishes.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tree House Restaurant in Santa Elena – a unique dining experience built around a 100-year-old fig tree, featuring international and Costa Rican cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Zip-line tours operate rain or shine – cloud forest weather is unpredictable but this adds to the mystical atmosphere. Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing. The quetzal is most active in the early morning – consider an optional pre-breakfast birdwatching walk for the chance to spot this elusive bird.

day_by_day.morning: Private birdwatching tour in Monteverde with a specialist ornithologist guide. Monteverde is considered one of the top birdwatching destinations in the world. Focus on spotting the resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbird, and rare endemic species. Use high-powered spotting scopes and binoculars provided by the guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Butterfly Garden, Orchid Garden, and Hummingbird Gallery in the Monteverde area – a trio of intimate nature exhibits showcasing the region's extraordinary biodiversity up close. Alternatively, visit the Selvatura Adventure Park for additional hanging bridges and wildlife exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Private chocolate and coffee tasting tour at a local organic farm. Learn about the bean-to-bar chocolate making process and Costa Rica's specialty coffee production. Enjoy a guided tasting paired with artisanal Monteverde cheeses and local wine.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge – light and quick before the morning birdwatching tour.
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at Hacienda Monteverde or a local organic farm restaurant.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Monteverde at Sofia Restaurant – sophisticated New Latin cuisine with a Costa Rican twist, featuring creative cocktails and an excellent wine list.

day_by_day.notes: This is the final full day in Monteverde. Pack and prepare for tomorrow's return journey. The chocolate tour typically lasts 1.5–2 hours and is a wonderful cultural and gastronomic experience unique to Costa Rica's agricultural heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Monteverde after breakfast via private luxury vehicle or charter flight to the Osa Peninsula / Corcovado region (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 1 hour by charter flight to Puerto Jiménez). Arrive and check into Lapa Rios Ecolodge or Playa Cativo Lodge – two of Costa Rica's most acclaimed luxury eco-lodges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon orientation and welcome at the lodge. Explore the lodge's private nature trails, enjoy the infinity pool overlooking the rainforest and ocean, or take a guided kayak tour through the nearby estuary spotting crocodiles and tropical birds.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the lodge's panoramic terrace. Private dinner at the lodge's open-air restaurant with sweeping views of the Golfo Dulce and surrounding primary rainforest.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Monteverde lodge before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch en route or at the lodge upon arrival – fresh ceviche, grilled fish, and tropical fruits.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lapa Rios or Playa Cativo Lodge restaurant – award-winning rainforest cuisine using hyper-local ingredients, featuring fresh Golfo Dulce seafood, organic vegetables, and tropical fruit desserts.

day_by_day.notes: Charter flight from Monteverde/San José to Puerto Jiménez is strongly recommended. The Osa Peninsula is one of the world's most biodiverse regions. This area is remote – embrace the off-grid luxury experience. Bring cash as ATMs are limited in Puerto Jiménez.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide. Depart early by boat or 4x4 vehicle to the park entrance. Venture deep into Corcovado, dubbed by National Geographic as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Trek through pristine primary rainforest with a certified naturalist guide. Encounter Baird's tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, giant anteaters, four species of monkeys, harpy eagles, and scarlet macaws.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado trek through diverse ecosystems including beach, river, and dense jungle. Swim in a natural jungle river pool or pristine Pacific beach within the park. The guide will provide expert interpretation of the ecosystem, tracks, and wildlife behavior.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge by late afternoon. Enjoy a restorative spa treatment – jungle botanical massage or rainforest mud wrap. Celebratory farewell dinner at the lodge with a special Costa Rican rum tasting to commemorate the adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early 05:30 breakfast at the lodge – high-energy meal before the full-day trek: eggs, gallo pinto, tropical fruits, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch prepared by the lodge chef – enjoyed in the jungle or on a pristine Corcovado beach: sandwiches, fresh fruit, energy bars, and purified water.
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the lodge – 5-course tasting menu celebrating Costa Rican biodiversity and cuisine, paired with premium Costa Rican rum and local craft beverages.

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado requires advance permits (SINAC permit) – the lodge or tour operator will arrange these. Wear long sleeves, sturdy hiking boots, and apply biodegradable insect repellent. Carry at least 3 liters of water. This is the most physically demanding day of the trip – it is one of the most extraordinary wildlife experiences in the world and absolutely worth the effort.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica. Leisurely sunrise walk on the lodge's private beach or a final birdwatching session on the property trails. Enjoy a long, indulgent farewell breakfast at the lodge. Pack and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Puerto Jiménez to San José (approximately 45 minutes) or direct connection depending on your departure flight. Arrive in San José with time to visit a premium artisan market or souvenir shop in the Escazú or San José area for last-minute gifts. Alternatively, enjoy a final lunch at a top San José restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) via private luxury vehicle. Depart Costa Rica with extraordinary memories of 13 days of eco-adventure, wildlife encounters, and luxury immersion in one of the world's most biodiverse countries.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the Osa Peninsula lodge – full spread of tropical fruits, artisanal pastries, eggs to order, and specialty Costa Rican coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch in San José – try Sikwa Restaurant (indigenous Costa Rican cuisine) or Park Café (award-winning creative cuisine) for a memorable final meal.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner in San José before departure, depending on flight schedule.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm charter flight and final private transfer 48 hours in advance. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for SJO airport check-in and security. Consider purchasing authentic Costa Rican coffee, chocolate, and local artisan crafts as souvenirs. Tip your guides, drivers, and lodge staff generously – gratuity is an important part of the local tourism economy.
